## Graphic Standards Manual

Week 1. Establish the graphic system used to communicate all later work.

- [Class 01]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-01/) — Week 1 — Aug 25: Begin the Graphic Standards Manual, test a sample sheet and organize your files.

<a id="b02"></a>

## Constructive Solid Geometry

Weeks 2–3. Build editable solids with transformations and Boolean operations.

- [Class 02 · Transformations and Booleans]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-02/) — Week 2 — Sep 1: Move, rotate and scale procedurally. Compare solid Boolean operators and begin the massing study.
- [Class 03 · 3D printing]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-03/) — Week 3 — Sep 8: Refine the CSG process sheet and instructions. Introduce P2b: prepare the CSG object for 3D printing, including units, orientation and slicing.

<a id="b03"></a>

## Descriptive Geometry

Weeks 4–5. Describe geometry through points, lines, edges and faces, then build a parametric solid.

- [Class 04 · Point to solid]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-04/) — Week 4 — Sep 15: Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean. Build the parametric pyramid and reconnect to the CSG project.
- [Class 05 · Your module, material and lighting]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-05/) — Week 5 — Sep 22: Build your own module from points and faces, test its parameter ranges, then render it with one material and a deliberate lighting setup for the P3a sheet.

<a id="b04"></a>

## Arrays 1 — loops in 1D, 2D and 3D

Week 6. First of two Arrays classes, paired with the loop tutorial. Use loops and nested loops to build a row, grid and layered array; explain counts, spacing and indices.

- [Class 06 · Arrays 1 — loops in 1D, 2D and 3D; CSG sheet]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-06/) — Week 6 — Sep 29: Submit 2.1 by 11:59 PM. Teach loops and nested loops through a 1D row, 2D grid and 3D layers, following the loop tutorial. Explain indices, counts and spacing. Check the CSG print before queueing.

<a id="b04-support"></a>

## Supported practice during studio reviews

Week 7. Optional help with work already introduced. No new topic or graded submission; this is not an additional Arrays class.

- Class 07 · Supported practice during studio reviews — *not yet released* — Week 7 — Oct 6: No graded submission. Optional help with module geometry, three-point lighting and small array tests.

<a id="b04-second"></a>

## Arrays 2 — if/Switch and math functions

Week 8. Second of two Arrays classes. Explain if/Switch selection through façade patterns, then use mathematical functions of X and Y to shape a cube volume. Hexagonal and radial arrays remain optional.

- Class 08 · Arrays 2 — if/Switch and math functions; CSG print — *not yet released* — Week 8 — Oct 13: Hand in 2.2 in class, with digital documentation by 11:59 PM. Teach if/Switch façade patterns and the cube volume driven by X and Y. Use small examples; hexagonal and radial arrays remain optional.

<a id="b05"></a>

## Façade attractors — Project 3

Week 9. One façade-attractor class. Combine one curve and one or two point attractors to drive a panel parameter. The next application of attractors is site analysis in Project 4.

- Class 09 · Façade attractors — Project 3; module deadline — *not yet released* — Week 9 — Oct 20: Submit 3.1. Teach the single façade-attractor class for 3.3, combining one curve and one or two points to drive a panel parameter. Begin the elevation and isometric composition.

<a id="b05-review"></a>

## Review of everything before Project 4

Week 10. Submit the manual and arrays. Review graphic standards, CSG/printing, panel construction, loops/arrays, if/Switch, mathematical functions and façade attractors together. Resolve gaps before the generative project. No new lecture topic, separate review assignment or additional grade.

- Class 10 · Review of everything; manual and arrays due — *not yet released* — Week 10 — Oct 27: Submit the manual and 3.2. Review graphic standards, CSG and printing, panel construction, loops/arrays, if/Switch, mathematical functions and the first curve/point façade response. Resolve gaps before Project 4. The review adds no separate submission or grade.

<a id="b06"></a>

## Attractor-based site analysis — Project 4

Week 11. Apply attractor measurements to the prepared point cloud using supplied groups. Produce two analytical layers and one design observation for the final project; this is distinct from the façade class.

- Class 11 · Attractor-based site analysis — Project 4 — *not yet released* — Week 11 — Nov 3: Begin 4.1: apply attractor measurements to the prepared point-cloud dataset using supplied analysis groups. Make two layers and one design observation. This class belongs to Project 4.

<a id="b06-volume"></a>

## Generative volume exploration — Project 4

Week 12. Use supplied volume groups to explore three settings of one strategy and select a form for contouring.

- Class 12 · Generative volumes — Project 4 — *not yet released* — Week 12 — Nov 10: Introduce 4.2 using supplied volume groups; explore three settings of one generative strategy and select an isometric result. Check the two site-analysis layers and provide façade feedback before its deadline.

<a id="b07"></a>

## Discretizing Geometry

Week 13. Use contours and sections to translate a volumetric design into parts for fabrication.

- Class 13 · Contouring and volume selection; façade deadline — *not yet released* — Week 13 — Nov 17: Submit 3.3. Select the generative volume at an ungraded check and introduce 4.3 using the supplied contouring group. Choose spacing, number the parts and prepare the cutting layout and assembly diagram.

<a id="b08"></a>

## Laser-cut model and final documentation

Weeks 14–15. Week 14 checks assembly tests and production plans. Week 15 offers fabrication and documentation support during studio reviews, with no graded submission.

- Class 14 · Assembly tests and laser-cut production; site deadline — *not yet released* — Week 14 — Nov 24: Submit 4.1. Check the 4.3 part layout and assembly test; introduce 4.4 and plan laser-cut production. Check a booklet spread. Use the session for fabrication decisions and troubleshooting.
- Class 15 · Connection tests, production and documentation — *not yet released* — Week 15 — Dec 1: No graded submission during studio reviews. Use ungraded support to check connections, part files, fabrication progress and final documentation.

## Possible intermediate class

<a id="o01"></a>

**Tessellation, panelization, lattices and simulation.** Offered only if time allows after arrays or attractors; no separate submission. The file covers tessellation and lattices. Panelization and simulation are possible additions. [Optional example files]({{ site.baseurl }}/resources/example-files/)
